staged_source_snapshot.description: Stage 01 reproduced against this staged vulnerable checkout, and the line locations below are grounded in this tree. `sample_info.json` names vulnerable commit `61dd44bbc1d7b98710ddd922b766170e55defe73`, but the prepared workspace used for the saved crash trace is the commit above (`v2.2-dev10-25-ga941952ae`). The vulnerable logic and staged patch still match the `src/cfgparse.c` branch ordering described below.

bug_description.original: OSS-Fuzz issue 42485221 (haproxy): Heap-buffer-overflow READ 1 found by fuzz target fuzz_cfg_parser [asan]. https://issues.oss-fuzz.com/issues/42485221
bug_description.original_source: sample_info.json / sanitizer_trace.txt / default_crash_trace.txt / reproduction_report.json / patch.diff / exact staged vulnerable source
bug_description.normalized: The staged reproducing checkout tokenizes each configuration line in `readcfgfile()` with `parse_line(line, outline, &outlen, args, &arg, ...)`, reusing heap buffer `outline` as the token storage backing `args[]`. `readcfgfile()` starts with `outlinesize = 0`; the first PoC line needs 14 output bytes, so the normal `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` retry allocates `outline` to 1024 bytes, and the second line leaves that allocation in place. On the crashing third line, tokenization needs 1196 output bytes and spans 65 whitespace-separated words, with the 64th stored word beginning at output offset 1168. `parse_line()` therefore keeps advancing `outpos` after setting `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE`, records `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1] = out + 1168` while that pointer is already outside the 1024-byte `outline`, and then sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` on the next separator. The vulnerable `readcfgfile()` checks `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` before the later `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP` branch that would `realloc(outline, (outlen + 1023) & -1024)`, so it formats `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` with `%s` in `ha_alert(...)` while the pointer is still out of bounds. `memvprintf()` then calls `vsnprintf()` on that variadic argument, and AddressSanitizer reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 in `printf_common`. The staged patch fixes this exact bug by moving the `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` alert block below the allocation-retry block.

source.var: line, outline, outlen, args, arg, err
source.description: Source. After `readcfgfile()` reads and trims the current attacker-controlled configuration line, this tokenizer call is the first project parser statement on the crashing path that materializes the vulnerability-relevant state: the token buffer extent `outlen`, the token pointers in `args[]`, and the error bits later tested by the bad alert branch.
source.value_from: The staged `poc` is a 1215-byte, 3-line HAProxy configuration witness written by the fuzz harness to `/tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>`, then parsed line by line by `readcfgfile()`. `readcfgfile()` starts with `outlinesize = 0`; the first 14-byte parsed line forces the normal retry allocation to 1024 bytes, and the crashing third line reaches this call reusing that 1024-byte `outline`. That third line tokenizes to 65 words and needs `outlen = 1196`, with the 64th stored word starting at output offset 1168.

sink.code: needed = vsnprintf(ret ? ret : &buf1, allocated, format, args);
sink.description: ASan-observed project sink. `memvprintf()` forwards the alert format string and varargs into `vsnprintf()`, which dereferences the out-of-bounds `%s` argument originating from `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]`.
sink.note: The saved sanitizer trace reports frame 0 in `printf_common` and frame 1 at this exact `memvprintf()` line.

root_cause.description: Root cause. When `parse_line()` returns both `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` and `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE`, `readcfgfile()` takes this branch before the later `if (err & (PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP))` block that would resize `outline` to `outlen`. It therefore computes and formats `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` while that pointer still lies beyond the current `outline` allocation. The staged patch fixes the bug by moving this whole `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` block below the allocation-retry branch.

tainted_value_origin.description: The tokenizer stores the start of the 64th parsed word as `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]`. In the staged witness this assignment records `outline + 1168` while the reused `outline` allocation is only 1024 bytes, creating the wild pointer later passed to `%s`.

parser_admitted.description: The harness has already written the witness to a temporary file and `readcfgfile()` has read the current line, stripped the trailing newline, and skipped leading spaces. Execution is now inside the configuration-line tokenizer used by the crashing path.

coarse_trace.summary: The fuzz harness writes the witness bytes to `/tmp/libfuzzer.<pid>` and calls `readcfgfile()` on that temporary file.
For each configuration line, `readcfgfile()` trims the line and invokes `parse_line()` with the reusable heap buffer `outline` that backs the `args[]` token pointers.

On the crashing line, tokenization both exceeds the current `outline` capacity and exceeds `MAX_LINE_ARGS`, so `parse_line()` records `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` past the end of `outline` and returns both `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` and `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY`.
The vulnerable caller handles `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` before the later reallocation branch and formats `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` with `%s` in `ha_alert()` while the pointer is still out of bounds.
`memvprintf()` calls `vsnprintf()` on that alert, and `%s` reads from the wild pointer, matching the saved AddressSanitizer heap-buffer-overflow READ.

fine_trace.var: line, outline, outlen, args, arg, err
fine_trace.note: Source. The current attacker-controlled configuration line enters HAProxy's tokenizer through this call. The returned `outlen`, `args[]`, and `err` are the exact parser outputs later consumed by the crashing alert path.

The first PoC line already grew `outline` to 1024 bytes. On the crashing third line, once `outpos` reaches that `outmax`, `parse_line()` sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` but still advances `outpos`. That preserves the full required length for retry while allowing later token starts to be computed past the current allocation.

On the separator ending the 63rd stored word, `arg` becomes 63 and the tokenizer records `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` as the start of the 64th word. In the staged witness this happens at `outpos == 1168`, so the stored pointer is 144 bytes past the current 1024-byte `outline` heap buffer.

At the next word separator, `arg` reaches 64, so `parse_line()` sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY`. The staged crashing line therefore has 65 words total, and the same parse now carries both `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE` from step 2 and `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` from this step.

Before returning to `readcfgfile()`, the tokenizer exports the final word count and the full required output length. For the staged crashing line this `outlen` is 1196, the size the later allocation-retry branch would use to resize `outline` for a retry.

Root cause. `readcfgfile()` handles `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` immediately and formats `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]` with `%s`, even though step 4 shows the same parse also needs the later `PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP` branch at lines 1985-1996 to `realloc(outline)` using step 5's `outlen`. The patch fixes the bug by moving this `TOOMANY` block below that allocation-retry block.

fine_trace.code: needed = vsnprintf(ret ? ret : &buf1, allocated, format, args);
fine_trace.note: Sink. The `ha_alert()` call from step 6 reaches `print_message()` and then `memvprintf()`, where `vsnprintf()` expands the `%s` argument using the out-of-bounds pointer created in step 3. The saved sanitizer trace reports the resulting heap-buffer-overflow READ of size 1 with frame 0 in `printf_common` and frame 1 at this line.

cross_validation.patch_resolves_note: The staged patch moves the `if (err & PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY)` alert block below the `if (err & (PARSE_ERR_TOOLARGE|PARSE_ERR_OVERLAP))` allocation-retry block, so the witnessed path reallocates `outline` before `%s` can consume `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1]`.

poc.trigger: The staged `poc` is a 1215-byte, 3-line HAProxy configuration witness. Its first line forces `readcfgfile()` to allocate the reusable `outline` buffer to 1024 bytes, and its crashing third line then tokenizes to 65 words and needs `outlen = 1196`, with the 64th stored word starting at output offset 1168. `readcfgfile()` then formats that already out-of-bounds `args[63]` pointer through the `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY` alert before the later resize branch runs.

format.name: HAProxy configuration
format.contract: The exact staged 3-line HAProxy configuration witness, or an equivalent witness-grounded input where `readcfgfile()` reaches the crashing line with a 1024-byte reusable `outline` buffer and that line tokenizes to 65 words with `outlen = 1196`, so the 64th stored word starts at output offset 1168. Under those specific conditions `parse_line()` stores `args[MAX_LINE_ARGS-1] = outline + 1168` before the next separator sets `PARSE_ERR_TOOMANY`, and the vulnerable `readcfgfile()` alert path dereferences that already out-of-bounds pointer before reallocating `outline`.
